reconstructed_theorem_text:
Define the local real-valued function F, for every positive natural number n, strictly positive real numbers beta and lambda, and real y, by
F(n, beta, lambda, y) = (n * beta^2 / lambda) * integral from 0 to (lambda * y / (n * beta)) of [g(2 - |s|) / (g(2 - |s|) + g(|s| - 1))] ds,
where g(t) = 0 for t <= 0 and g(t) = exp(-1/t) for t > 0. Here n is coerced to a real number, and the interval integral uses real Lebesgue measure with oriented endpoints.
For every type Omega equipped with any measurable-space structure, every measure P on Omega, every positive natural number n, every pair of strictly positive real numbers beta and lambda, every function Y: Omega -> R, and every nonnegative real number v, suppose Y is almost everywhere measurable with respect to P and the pushforward of P under Y is the Gaussian probability law with mean 0 and variance v. For every real a with 0 <= a <= 1, the function omega |-> exp(-a * F(n, beta, lambda, Y(omega))) is integrable with respect to P, and
integral over Omega of exp(-a * F(n, beta, lambda, Y(omega))) dP(omega) <= exp(beta^2 * Var_P(Y) / 2).
Integrability asserts almost everywhere strong measurability and finite integral of the norm; the displayed integral is a real Bochner integral. Var_P(Y) is the real-valued variance under P (equal to v under the stated Gaussian-law hypothesis). The case v = 0 is included and means that the Gaussian law is the Dirac law at 0.
objects: The explicitly defined local function F; the fixed piecewise function g; a measurable space Omega; a measure P; parameters n, beta, lambda, v, a; a real-valued function Y on Omega; the Gaussian law of mean 0 and variance v; the integrand exp(-a * F(n, beta, lambda, Y(omega))); and the real-valued variance Var_P(Y).
domains: Omega is any type with any measurable-space structure. P is a measure on Omega. n is a positive natural number. beta and lambda are strictly positive reals. Y maps Omega to R. v belongs to the nonnegative reals, including zero. a is real and lies in the closed interval [0, 1]. The local definition of F accepts every real y, and its integration variable s is real.
quantifiers: The local definition of F precedes the whole proposition. Universally quantify, in displayed order, Omega and its measurable-space structure, P, n, beta, lambda, Y, v, a proof of the Gaussian-law hypothesis, a, and a proof that a belongs to [0, 1]. Equivalently, for every such Omega, structure, P, n, beta, lambda, Y, v satisfying the law hypothesis, and every a in [0, 1], both asserted conclusions hold. Omega, Y, and a are implicit Lean arguments but remain universally quantified. The y and s in F and omega in the conclusion are locally bound.
assumptions: n >= 1, beta > 0, lambda > 0, v >= 0, and 0 <= a <= 1. The Gaussian-law hypothesis is exactly that Y is P-almost-everywhere measurable and Measure.map Y P equals the Gaussian probability measure with mean 0 and variance v. No separate probability-measure assumption on P, pointwise measurability assumption on Y, positive-variance assumption, or integrability assumption is added.
conclusion: The conjunction of (1) P-integrability of omega |-> exp(-a * F(n, beta, lambda, Y(omega))) and (2) its real Bochner integral with respect to P being at most exp(beta^2 * Var_P(Y) / 2). Integrability includes almost everywhere strong measurability and finite integral of the norm.
scopes: F is a literal local definition with exactly the displayed full body; it is not an arbitrary function satisfying additional properties. Its n, beta, lambda, y binders are local to that definition. The subsequent quantified n, beta, lambda are supplied as arguments to F, and Y(omega) is its fourth argument. Both conclusions are under all the same hypotheses, including both endpoints of [0, 1]. The factor -a multiplies the entire value of F in the exponential. The complete upper bound is exp of beta^2 times variance divided by 2.
constant_dependencies: The bound is exactly exp(beta^2 * Var_P(Y) / 2): its right-hand side has no explicit dependence on n, lambda, or a, and its dependence on v is through Var_P(Y), which equals v under the law hypothesis. The constant 1/2 is fixed, not existential. F uses the fixed cutoff constants 1 and 2, exponent 2 on beta, lower endpoint 0, and g(t) = exp(-1/t) on positive t with value 0 otherwise. There are no unspecified constants or hidden parameter restrictions.
